neighbours.label: ' parts' after a verb of dividing into a number ('divided into two parts', 'split into three parts')
fire: The old town is divided into two parts by a narrow canal.
We split the workshop into three parts so everyone could rest.
The novel is broken into four parts, each told by a different sister.
After the war the province was cut into two parts along the river.
The exam is divided into two parts: a written test and an interview.
She folded the letter and tore it into several parts.
The course splits naturally into two parts, theory and practice.
The cake was cut into eight equal parts for the guests.
quiet: The old town is crossed by a narrow canal with many bridges.
We split the workshop into three sessions so everyone could rest.
The novel is broken into four chapters, each told by a different sister.
After the war the province was cut into two halves along the river.
The mechanic ordered spare parts for the old tractor yesterday.
She folded the letter and put it in her coat pocket.
In some parts of the country it snows every winter.
The cake was cut into eight equal slices for the guests.

notes: Card: ' parts' x13, nearly all after 'divided/split/broken into two'; also 'two', 'three', 'smaller'. Near misses: the division with another noun, and 'parts' without division.
